utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Tustin' by name among the cities in its service area.

generation_supplier.notes: Orange County Power Authority (OCPA), the CCA operating in Orange County, currently names Buena Park, Fullerton, and Irvine as members (with Fountain Valley reported joining in 2027) — Tustin was not named among current or announced members this session. Left null rather than asserted either way.

county.notes: Tustin is a well-documented Orange County city; also listed under Orange County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.value: City of Tustin Community Development Department

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Tustin/Orange County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Site layout plan and single-line diagram

value: Schedule through the CSS account by selecting 'Inspections'
Request must be made by 3:00pm the prior business day for next-day inspection
Call inspectors between 7:30am and 8:00am on the inspection day for a timeframe, using the phone numbers on the job card

value.program_or_pathway: SolarAPP+ (residential, roof-mounted, retrofit PV) / traditional review (all other projects)
other_conditions: Properties within the Cultural Resource District (CRD) or listed on the city's Historic Resource Survey as an eligible individual property are not eligible for the SolarAPP+ streamlining program and must use traditional review
Permit types include standalone solar, solar with battery, solar with panel upgrade, or solar with battery and panel upgrade

permit_fees.notes: The page states city fees are required at application and SolarAPP+ charges separate processing fees, but no dollar figures are given.
